nodes.label: Authority-Aware Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Statute, regulation, binding opinion and nonprecedential guidance are not interchangeable even when equally semantically relevant; authority is used both as a rerank signal and in answer presentation. Gaps surface as 'authority unknown', never silently defaulted to a safe level.

nodes.label: Post-Generation Claim Verification
nodes.rationale: The synthesized answer is decomposed into atomic claims, each checked against its cited source by a self-hosted NLI model producing entailed/neutral/contradicted. Entailment is not correctness: a claim can be entailed and still be the wrong answer if the source is lower authority, wrong jurisdiction, superseded, or omits a controlling exception.

nodes.label: Evidence-Sufficiency Gate
nodes.rationale: Refuses a sub-question whose retrieved evidence is too thin, before generating rather than after.

nodes.label: Hybrid Retrieval (Dense + Sparse)
nodes.rationale: Legal text needs literal matching of exact terms (§280A, Form 8829) alongside meaning, so dense and BM25-style sparse vectors are fused in one Qdrant query.

nodes.label: Phase A Known Failures
nodes.rationale: Five documented failures: illustrative text out-competing the rule it illustrates, a plausible near-miss on leased cars, publication dilution, the dead-publication closed-book citation, and every partial grade carrying the same missing_condition defect tag (39 of 39).

nodes.label: Log #5: Corpus Gaps Shape the Evaluation
nodes.norm_label: log #5: corpus gaps shape the evaluation
nodes.rationale: There is no §1.280A in eCFR — the home-office regulations were proposed but never finalized — and the PRD's headline example is a home-office question, so it depends on Pub 587 and the statute rather than regulations.

nodes.label: Log #24: Adding a Second Corpus Made Retrieval Worse
nodes.norm_label: log #24: adding a second corpus made retrieval worse
nodes.rationale: Hybrid recall fell 0.812 to 0.688 on the same 16 regulation questions when IRS publications were added, because publications are written in the same plain English as the question and semantic similarity rewards the paraphrase over the binding law. Keep both corpora and do not hand-tune: this is precisely the failure authority-aware reranking exists to fix, now with a measured baseline to beat.

nodes.label: Log #14: Table-of-Contents Sections Would Poison Retrieval
nodes.norm_label: log #14: table-of-contents sections would poison retrieval
nodes.rationale: 178 sections (~4% of Part 1) are nothing but headings of other sections; embedded, a block of 40 topic headings is a weak match for almost any query on those topics and competes with the rule text on every query. Near-duplicate, high-surface-area documents hurt retrieval even when accurate, and finding them takes looking at the corpus rather than the metrics.

nodes.label: ADR-1: Decomposition + Bounded Citation-Graph Traversal
nodes.rationale: A bounded 1-2 hop citation-graph expansion on the case-law sub-query beats decomposition alone on multi-hop legal reasoning, without the infrastructure cost of full GraphRAG community detection this corpus does not need.

nodes.label: ADR-10: Batch the Sufficiency Gate Into One Call Per Sub-Query
nodes.norm_label: adr-10: batch the sufficiency gate into one call per sub-query
nodes.rationale: Per-candidate judging cost up to top_k x 3 LLM calls, the most expensive and slowest step. One structured-output call per sub-query drops it to 3, accepting anchoring/averaging risk mitigated by requiring a per-candidate field in the output schema.

nodes.label: ADR-3: Post-Generation Claim Verification
nodes.rationale: A claim-decomposition plus NLI-entailment pass is kept independent of the evidence-sufficiency gate because the two catch different failure modes; it proves support, not legal correctness.

nodes.label: ADR-7: Sufficiency Gate Runs Before Synthesis
nodes.norm_label: adr-7: sufficiency gate runs before synthesis
nodes.rationale: Running the gate after synthesis meant generating over evidence that might then be discarded. Moving it before synthesis requires synthesis to handle partial input, in exchange for never generating then retracting unsupported content.

nodes.label: ADR-8: Authority-Aware Reranking
nodes.rationale: Purely semantic reranking lets a nonprecedential IRS publication outrank a controlling statute. Authority becomes an explicit rerank signal, at the cost of depending on authority metadata that is itself a source of extraction error.

nodes.label: Citation-Graph Traversal
nodes.rationale: Opinions cite, distinguish and overrule each other, which hierarchical decomposition misses; a bounded 1-2 hop expansion along CITES/DISTINGUISHES/OVERRULES/AMENDS surfaces precedent similarity-only search cannot.

nodes.label: Ablation Ladder
nodes.rationale: Each stage from closed-book through claim verification is isolated so the report shows what each mechanism actually contributes, not just the final system's aggregate score.

nodes.label: IRS Publications and Guidance
nodes.rationale: No structured API exists; a rate-limited scraper with an identifying user-agent respecting robots.txt is the standard approach for the one ingestion source that genuinely requires scraping.

nodes.norm_label: t4: pilot set and retrieval eval script

nodes.label: Log #29: The Closed-Book Baseline Cited a Publication That No Longer Exists
nodes.norm_label: log #29: the closed-book baseline cited a publication that no longer exists
nodes.rationale: On the first question asked, closed-book recommended IRS Pub 535 — discontinued after 2022. The plausible kind of hallucination: a real number, right topic, gone three years. Paragraph-level vs section-level citation, verifiable vs not, live vs dead is a sharper argument than a groundedness percentage because a reviewer can check it in a minute.

nodes.label: Log #23: A Discontinued Publication Returns HTTP 200 With HTML
nodes.norm_label: log #23: a discontinued publication returns http 200 with html
nodes.rationale: Pub 535's URL still returns 200 and redirects to an HTML page, which the ingest saved as a .pdf and only failed on later inside the parser. Verify content, not status code: a download whose first bytes are not %PDF- is deleted and reported. A 200 is not proof you got what you asked for.

nodes.label: Log #21: Gold Sets Need Validating Before They Can Validate Anything
nodes.norm_label: log #21: gold sets need validating before they can validate anything
nodes.rationale: The author is not a tax professional, so 'these look right' was unavailable. Two safeguards: every reference answer paraphrases one specific paragraph so checking is reading comprehension, and a validator runs before any scoring. It caught a wrong gold citation, a missing material condition, and an over-generic citation.

nodes.label: Log #19: Hybrid Retrieval Is Not Uniformly Better Than Dense
nodes.norm_label: log #19: hybrid retrieval is not uniformly better than dense
nodes.rationale: A real bug came first: sparse vectors were created without Qdrant's IDF modifier, so common legal words scored like rare ones. After the fix, which mode wins depends on query shape. Ship all three modes as ablation rungs and let the pilot set decide, rather than tuning fusion by eye on one query.

nodes.label: Log #20: Measurement Overturned What One Query Suggested
nodes.norm_label: log #20: measurement overturned what one query suggested
nodes.rationale: Split by query style, sparse is perfect on keyword questions and poor on natural-language ones, dense is the mirror image, and hybrid inherits the better half of each — the actual argument for hybrid, visible only when questions are split by style. The gap between section recall 1.000 and strict recall 0.812 is the reranking budget, quantified before the work starts.

nodes.label: Log #16: Parallel Workers Made Embedding Slower
nodes.norm_label: log #16: parallel workers made embedding slower
nodes.rationale: 7.0 chunks/s single-process vs 3.4/s at four workers, because the ONNX runtime already threads across cores and extra processes contend plus add spawn and serialisation overhead. The measured numbers live in the docstring so nobody optimises it back.

nodes.label: Log #22: Choosing a PDF Library by Measuring It on the Real Document
nodes.norm_label: log #22: choosing a pdf library by measuring it on the real document
nodes.rationale: pypdf's default mode broke words apart and its layout mode interleaved the two columns into plausible-looking nonsense; pdfminer.six produced zero broken words and correct column order. The failure mode that matters, silently garbled sentences, is invisible unless you read the extracted text — both pypdf modes 'worked' in the sense of returning text.

nodes.label: Log #25: Screen Candidates for Viability Before Measuring Quality
nodes.norm_label: log #25: screen candidates for viability before measuring quality
nodes.rationale: A model that might have scored better never got a quality score, which is the right order: quality on an unusable model is a number you cannot act on. The exclusion reason is written into the benchmark file so it reads as a decision rather than an oversight.

nodes.label: The Pilot Set Is Data, Not Code
nodes.norm_label: the pilot set is data, not code
nodes.rationale: eval/pilot.jsonl holds question, gold section citations and a reference answer; the eval scripts stay small and live next to it.

nodes.label: Non-Goals (no full GraphRAG, no BM25 engine, no token streaming, federal only)
nodes.norm_label: non-goals (no full graphrag, no bm25 engine, no token streaming, federal only)

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.rationale: Serves three roles: caching statute lookups and as-of query results, caching full verified sub-answers as the primary cost lever, and carrying live SSE progress events.

nodes.label: Phase A Implementation Plan
nodes.rationale: The exit condition is evidence plus a runnable path: a reviewer can POST a question, watch the SSE stage events and get a cited answer, with the pilot numbers written down.

nodes.label: T9: Job Record and SSE Transport
nodes.norm_label: t9: job record and sse transport

nodes.label: Log #11: Stay True to the Architecture, Defer Stores Until They Have Work
nodes.norm_label: log #11: stay true to the architecture, defer stores until they have work
nodes.rationale: All five stores stay in the architecture, but Phase A runs only Qdrant, Postgres and Redis. Neo4j arrives with the citation graph and Langfuse with tracing, so nothing idle gets operated or debugged.

nodes.label: Log #9: Redis vs Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY for Live Events
nodes.norm_label: log #9: redis vs postgres listen/notify for live events
nodes.rationale: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY would remove a store and let the job-state update and event share a transaction, but Supabase's pooled connections do not support LISTEN and each SSE stream would hold a scarce direct connection. Redis also gives cache expiry the cost ceiling depends on. Self-hosted Postgres would have made it close to a coin flip.

nodes.label: Log #10: Keep Live Delivery Separate From Tracing
nodes.norm_label: log #10: keep live delivery separate from tracing
nodes.rationale: Two writes per step in exchange for independent failures: a Langfuse outage costs dashboard data, never the answer the user is waiting on.

nodes.label: Log #12: Vercel Is the Wrong Host for This Backend
nodes.norm_label: log #12: vercel is the wrong host for this backend
nodes.rationale: A query runs 20-30s across several LLM calls, needs a worker that outlives the request, holds an SSE stream open, and depends on self-hosted stores and an NLI model. Serverless is at most for the thin frontend.

nodes.label: Simplify Inside Components, Never By Dropping a Store
nodes.norm_label: simplify inside components, never by dropping a store
nodes.rationale: The architecture stays as specified under a 3-4 month / <$50-per-month constraint; simplification happens inside components (fewest abstractions, standard library first), never by dropping a store or an ADR.

nodes.label: Host Port Offsets (5433 / 6380)
nodes.rationale: Postgres is published on 5433 and Redis on 6380 because local installs already own 5432 and 6379; avoids a port clash on the developer machine.

nodes.label: Plain-Module Package Layout
nodes.rationale: src/taxcite/ with plain modules and no framework layers; each stage is one function, and where a model is swappable the choice is one config value, not an interface hierarchy.

nodes.label: ADR-16: Live Delivery Decoupled From Tracing
nodes.norm_label: adr-16: live delivery decoupled from tracing
nodes.rationale: Sourcing live SSE events from Langfuse spans coupled the product's live delivery to an observability tool's uptime. Publishing progress to Redis costs one extra write per step and buys separate failure domains: a Langfuse outage degrades dashboards, never the answer a user is waiting on.

nodes.label: ADR-6: Qdrant Native Sparse+Dense Hybrid, Not Meilisearch
nodes.norm_label: adr-6: qdrant native sparse+dense hybrid, not meilisearch
nodes.rationale: Meilisearch was mislabeled as 'the BM25 layer' — it uses a proprietary multi-criteria ranking. Qdrant's native hybrid removes a datastore and fixes the terminology; legal text needs literal matching of terms like §280A alongside meaning.

nodes.label: ADR-9: SSE Progress Stream Over a Durable Job Record
nodes.norm_label: adr-9: sse progress stream over a durable job record
nodes.rationale: A 15-30s multi-stage pipeline with several terminal outcomes cannot sit behind synchronous request/response (free-tier proxy idle timeouts sit on top of worst-case latency, and a dropped connection loses several paid LLM calls). Polling fights per-stage progress. The answer is buffered, never token-streamed, so an unverified claim never reaches a credentialed preparer.

nodes.label: Postgres Service (pgvector/pgvector:pg16)
nodes.community_name: ADR-17: Vector Store — Qdrant, Not pgvector
nodes.rationale: The image is pgvector/pgvector:pg16 rather than plain postgres:16 so the T6b ADR-17 benchmark can load the same vectors into pgvector without a second container.

nodes.label: pgvector
nodes.community_name: ADR-17: Vector Store — Qdrant, Not pgvector
nodes.rationale: The strongest alternative to Qdrant: it removes a store and keeps text, metadata and vector in one row so they cannot drift. It loses on hand-written fusion SQL, post-filtering that can silently return fewer than k, and managed free-tier storage caps.

nodes.label: T6b: Qdrant vs pgvector Benchmark
nodes.community_name: ADR-17: Vector Store — Qdrant, Not pgvector
nodes.rationale: Vectors go in a separate bench_chunks table and bench_* collections so app tables and the live collection are untouched by the benchmark.

nodes.label: Log #17: Chunker Output Is 12x the Section Count
nodes.community_name: ADR-17: Vector Store — Qdrant, Not pgvector
nodes.norm_label: log #17: chunker output is 12x the section count
nodes.rationale: 3,774 sections become 44,250 chunks, one per 85 words. More, smaller chunks make retrieval sharper and citations precise, at the cost of a bigger index, longer embedding, and a harder reranking job.

nodes.label: Log #8: Qdrant Over pgvector, With a Measurable Revisit Trigger
nodes.community_name: ADR-17: Vector Store — Qdrant, Not pgvector
nodes.norm_label: log #8: qdrant over pgvector, with a measurable revisit trigger
nodes.rationale: ADR-6 picked Qdrant but never said why it beat other vector stores; an interviewer's first question would be 'why not pgvector in the Postgres you already run?'. What makes the decision defensible is a falsifiable revisit trigger backed by a planned benchmark.

nodes.label: ADR-17: Vector Store — Qdrant, Not pgvector
nodes.community_name: ADR-17: Vector Store — Qdrant, Not pgvector
nodes.norm_label: adr-17: vector store — qdrant, not pgvector
nodes.rationale: ADR-6 settled Qdrant vs a lexical engine but never why Qdrant beat other vector stores. Four requirements: single-query hybrid fusion, filtering applied during the ANN search, free self-hosting, one-engineer operability. Confirmed by T6b measurement: the deciding gap is lexical (BM25 0.444 vs ts_rank_cd 0.111), not dense and not filtering (0.779 in both). The originally written revisit trigger was mis-specified — both its conditions passed — and gained the condition that mattered: hybrid recall within 2 points.

nodes.label: 100-Question Golden Set
nodes.rationale: Stratified (25 statutory, 20 case-law, 30 compound, 10 temporal, 10 expected-insufficiency, 5 adversarial) so no single question type dominates the aggregate score.

nodes.label: nomic-embed-text-v1.5
nodes.rationale: Excluded on latency before any quality measurement: 0.2 chunks/s and 491 ms per query embed, for an 8192-token context the corpus never uses.

nodes.label: Phase B — Decomposition + Eval Infrastructure
nodes.rationale: RAGAS is wired into CI as a standing regression gate on every future PR touching retrieval, prompts, reranking or verification, not a one-time checkbox; build fails below 0.85 faithfulness.

nodes.label: Phase A Exit Report
nodes.rationale: Every number is reproducible from eval/ against the running stack; nothing is estimated.

nodes.label: Phase A Recalibration Notes for §9.3
nodes.rationale: Phase A's thresholds were set before any data existed; the measurements suggest a completeness metric may bind before entailment does, since missing_condition dominates defects.

nodes.label: Acceptance Thresholds by Phase (§9.3)
nodes.rationale: First-pass engineering targets set before any real measurement existed; they exist to be recalibrated against Phase A-H data, not treated as final commitments.

nodes.label: Log #26: The Benchmark Died Because of Unrelated Software
nodes.norm_label: log #26: the benchmark died because of unrelated software
nodes.rationale: 17 containers from an unrelated demo stack held load average at 6-12 and a bulk upsert exceeded the client's short default timeout, surfacing as a one-word 'timed out' 20 minutes into a job. Raise the timeout to 120s and retry with backoff rather than treating a slow host as fatal; re-measure on a quiet machine rather than salvaging the first run.

nodes.label: Log #28: One Tied Score Made the Eval Unreproducible
nodes.norm_label: log #28: one tied score made the eval unreproducible
nodes.rationale: Exactly one question flipped between runs, its gold chunk tied at rank 10 of 10, so whichever the store kept at the cut decided the hit. Over-fetch 20 extra and break ties by citation before truncating, so the cut happens in our code deterministically. It also sets the floor on what the pilot set can resolve — one question is 5.6 points — which is the concrete argument for the 100-question golden set.

nodes.label: ADR-18: Dense Embedding Model — BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5
nodes.rationale: Chosen because ranking gains exceed recall gains (nDCG +9, dense MRR +13) and synthesis only sees the top few chunks; it recovers about half the 12.4-point publication dilution. Trade-off: 3.4x index time and 2x storage, so any re-index now costs half an hour. The hybrid gap (+5.6) sits at the pilot set's resolution limit, so the decision rests on the deterministic dense metrics.

nodes.label: Query Decomposition
nodes.rationale: A compound tax question is split into statutory, case-law and client-fact sub-queries so each is retrieved with the right corpus and technique, rather than one undifferentiated similarity search.

nodes.label: T8: ADR-11 LLM Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Capped at 20 questions x <=3 models x 2 modes with the script printing running cost and stopping at a configurable limit, so benchmark spend cannot run away.

nodes.label: Log #31: The Reliability Check Measured Two Standards and Called It Noise
nodes.norm_label: log #31: the reliability check measured two standards and called it noise
nodes.rationale: Giving the second judge a stricter rubric is a second standard, not a second reading of the same one; kappa came out 0.65 with 9 of 13 disagreements in exactly the direction a stricter prompt forces. Same rubric neutrally reworded took kappa to 0.81. Temperature would have been the cleaner knob but current Anthropic models reject sampling parameters, so paraphrasing keeps the method identical across providers. A failed threshold can be a finding about the instrument, not the system — the tell was the direction of disagreements, not their number.

nodes.label: Log #27: The Revisit Trigger I Wrote Was Mis-Specified
nodes.norm_label: log #27: the revisit trigger i wrote was mis-specified
nodes.rationale: Both conditions of the trigger passed, and filtered recall was identical, disproving the assumption the trigger was written around. The deciding number — lexical ranking, 0.111 vs 0.444 — was not in the trigger at all. A falsifiable trigger is better than an unexamined decision, but writing one is itself a design act that can be wrong: it tested the hypothesis the author happened to have instead of the property that mattered.

nodes.label: Log #30: The Two Models Fail in Different Directions
nodes.norm_label: log #30: the two models fail in different directions
nodes.rationale: gpt-4o-mini grades higher but cites sparsely; claude-haiku grades lower, cites heavily, fabricates nothing and lands the gold citation twice as often. For a product whose thesis is verifiable citations, 'grades worse, cites better' is not obviously the worse model. Abstention also appeared from prompt instructions alone, before the sufficiency gate exists.

nodes.label: Three-Way Citation Counting
nodes.rationale: Citations are counted as exact / derived (a narrower paragraph of a retrieved section) / fabricated, because collapsing them misread haiku as inventing citations.

nodes.label: ADR-11: LLM Tiering — gpt-4o-mini
nodes.rationale: Decided 2026-09-21 from the T8 benchmark. Cost turned out not to be the binding constraint (~$0.10/mo at persona volume against a $50 ceiling), so the decision rests on quality: gpt-4o-mini is 0.61 vs 0.33 correct, never outright wrong under RAG, ~3x faster, ~8x cheaper. The uncomfortable half: haiku grades worse but cites better (gold citation on 50% vs 33%, zero fabrications, refused both unanswerable questions). Accepted because Phase F's NLI verifier checks claims mechanically, a stronger guarantee than citing habits. Revisit trigger: move synthesis to claude-haiku-4-5 if Phase F suppresses too much for want of citations.

nodes.label: ADR-15: Zero-Tolerance Claim Suppression
nodes.rationale: Inline flagging of unentailed claims was replaced by full suppression of any sub-answer containing a single failed claim. More sub-answers are suppressed than under a threshold approach, but no partially-trusted content ever reaches the user and no standing UI disclaimer is needed.

nodes.label: ADR-4: Self-Hosted NLI Model for Production Verification
nodes.norm_label: adr-4: self-hosted nli model for production verification
nodes.rationale: A specialized self-hosted NLI checkpoint is cheaper and faster than a per-claim LLM call; LLM-as-judge is reserved for the offline harness, with a periodic audit at F1 >= 0.90 mitigating the loss of nuance.

nodes.label: Substantive-Correctness Grading Protocol (§9.2)
nodes.rationale: With no budget for manual labeling, an LLM judge from a different provider than the generator applies a 3-point rubric, with a second differently-configured judge and Cohen's kappa >= 0.70 standing in for inter-rater reliability. The stated limitation is correlated error: an AI judge can share the generator's blind spots on exactly the failure modes the metric exists to catch.

nodes.label: Phase H — Resilience + Load
nodes.rationale: 'Realistic concurrency' is scoped to the actual persona — dozens of questions per week — so k6 targets a generous multiple of that, not market-scale concurrent-user assumptions.

nodes.label: Production SLOs and Alerting (§3.4)
nodes.rationale: p95 <=35s synthesis / <=2s refusal, error rate <1%. Store health-check alerts fire even where the system degrades gracefully, because graceful degradation should be visible to the operator, not just to the user.

nodes.label: ADR-12: Backup and Disaster Recovery
nodes.rationale: A single engineer operates five stateful services on free-tier infra with no stated recovery plan. Nightly pg_dump, neo4j-admin dump and Qdrant snapshots with 14-day retention, plus a quarterly restore drill, because a dump that was produced is not a dump that is restorable.

nodes.label: Single-Engineer Operational Bus Factor
nodes.rationale: Five self-hosted stateful services run solo on free-tier infra. Backup drills mitigate data loss but not availability during the operator's own downtime — named explicitly rather than assuming free-tier hosting implies free-tier operational risk.

nodes.label: Collaborative Working Mode
nodes.rationale: Claude writes the code and may edit existing files; new files are handed over as code blocks for the user to create.

nodes.label: Bi-Temporal Fact Validity
nodes.rationale: Valid time (effective_date/superseded_date/superseded_by) records when the rule applied; transaction time (recorded_at/retired_at) records when TaxCite believed it. Amendments create a new versioned node rather than overwriting.

nodes.label: Per-Document-Type Chunker (§3.2)
nodes.rationale: Statute gets section-level 200-500 token chunks because section boundaries are already semantically complete and mirror legal citation granularity; case law gets paragraph-level chunks with one-paragraph overlap to preserve cross-paragraph reference resolution.

nodes.label: CourtListener
nodes.rationale: Free-tier REST access was cut from 5,000 req/hr to 125/day in May 2026, so initial bulk load uses the quarterly CSV dumps and the API is reserved for weekly incremental pulls.

nodes.label: eCFR API (26 CFR)
nodes.rationale: No key required, daily updates, and it already tracks point-in-time section history, which maps directly onto the bi-temporal model — the strongest single data source in the pipeline.

nodes.label: GovInfo (GPO)
nodes.rationale: Used only for weekly change detection via its modified-since endpoint, not for content; its USCOURTS collection is also a rate-limit-independent supplement to CourtListener.

nodes.label: uscode.house.gov (OLRC)
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the statute content source because it is one hop from the source of truth, its release points are tied to enacted Public Laws (a better fit for bi-temporal than annual editions), and it is a static download with no rate-limited API on the content path.

nodes.label: Nine-Section eCFR Test Fixture
nodes.rationale: Nine real sections (58 KB), each chosen because it breaks a specific naive assumption: a range section number, a reserved section, packing with an EXAMPLE, a combined two-level designation, (i) as a letter, (i) as a Roman numeral, an oversized table, and a table of contents.

nodes.label: T2: Ingest eCFR Title 26
nodes.rationale: Scoped to 21 section prefixes (~5,000 chunks, 13 min) instead of all of Part 1 (43,583 chunks, ~105 min), to keep the T6 model-comparison loop fast; the full run waits until the embedding model is chosen.

nodes.label: Log #1: Spec Chunk Size Didn't Survive the Data
nodes.norm_label: log #1: spec chunk size didn't survive the data
nodes.rationale: The design doc's 200-500 token section chunks assumed legal citation granularity, but 26 CFR Part 1 has a median ~1,350 tokens per section and 74% over 500. An hour of exploration before writing any parser bought avoiding a parser built on a false assumption.

nodes.label: Log #18: The Counts-Match Check Caught Silent Data Loss
nodes.norm_label: log #18: the counts-match check caught silent data loss
nodes.rationale: 154 chunks vanished with no error because sections embedding their own outline in an EXTRACT restarted paragraph numbering, so eleven chunks claimed one citation and the upsert overwrote them. The boring invariant found the bug 40 passing unit tests missed, because it was the only check comparing what went in with what came out. EXTRACT became an opaque block and part is renumbered per citation so keys are unique by construction, not assumption.

nodes.label: Log #13: The iCloud Bug That Broke Editable Installs
nodes.norm_label: log #13: the icloud bug that broke editable installs
nodes.rationale: Two harmless macOS behaviours combined: iCloud Desktop sync sets UF_HIDDEN recursively inside .venv/, and CPython 3.13+ silently skips hidden .pth files, which editable installs depend on entirely. Found with ls -lO; the lasting fix is keeping projects outside iCloud sync in *.nosync folders rather than re-applying a chflags workaround.

nodes.label: Log #4: Italic Designations Are a Different Hierarchy Level
nodes.norm_label: log #4: italic designations are a different hierarchy level
nodes.rationale: Stripping markup before parsing would make level-5 (2) look like level-2 (2) and split at the wrong places. Markup carries meaning; normalizing text too early loses information.

nodes.label: Log #2: Chunk at Paragraph Designations, Two Levels Deep
nodes.norm_label: log #2: chunk at paragraph designations, two levels deep
nodes.rationale: Legal citations already point at paragraph units, so the document's own structure gives better boundaries than a token counter. Depth stops at two levels because going deeper means resolving ambiguous designations ((i), (v), (x) are both letters and Roman numerals) — deferred until retrieval evaluation shows deeper citations matter.

nodes.label: Log #15: Fixtures From Real Edge Cases, Not Invented
nodes.norm_label: log #15: fixtures from real edge cases, not invented
nodes.rationale: Scanning the real corpus turned up edge cases no hand-written fixture would contain (range section numbers, reserved stubs, designation ranges, and the two opposite readings of (i)). A bigger messier fixture, in exchange for every test failure corresponding to a real document that exists.

nodes.label: Log #7: Origin for Content, Mirror for Change Detection
nodes.norm_label: log #7: origin for content, mirror for change detection
nodes.rationale: Two sources instead of one, in return for staying one hop from the source of truth, versions tied to real enacted law changes, and no rate-limited API on the content path — a lesson taken from CourtListener cutting its free tier.

nodes.label: Log #3: Tables — A Few Huge, Many Small and Meaningful
nodes.norm_label: log #3: tables — a few huge, many small and meaningful
nodes.rationale: Flatten tables of <=100 cells (90%+ of them); larger ones get no embedding and are recorded with reason large_table. Actuarial tables become unfindable by semantic search, acceptable because they are lookup data a future structured tool can query, and recording them keeps the gap visible instead of hidden.

nodes.label: Log #6: The Source XML Already Carries Temporal Signals
nodes.norm_label: log #6: the source xml already carries temporal signals
nodes.rationale: CITA lists every amendment with its Treasury Decision number and date and marks redesignations. Storing it raw now, plus the as-of date and download time on every chunk, costs two columns instead of a migration later.

nodes.label: Approximate Search Loses 22% Under a Strict Filter
nodes.norm_label: approximate search loses 22% under a strict filter
nodes.rationale: Unplanned finding: approximate search returns only 77.9% of the exact top-10 under a strict single-section filter, in both Qdrant and pgvector. Phase D's as-of filtering is the same shape and will need exact search or a raised ef_search rather than default ANN parameters.

nodes.label: eCFR Chunking Decisions
nodes.rationale: Split at paragraph level 1 and at level 2 only above ~500 tokens; keep short sections whole and never merge across sections; skip reserved paragraphs and TOC sections; flatten tables <=100 cells; store CITA raw; keep as-of date and download time. Each chunk carries a source field so corpora stay separable for filtering and the T6b filtered-search benchmark. No tenant field: 26 CFR is the shared public corpus.

nodes.label: ADR-13: Sanitized Rendering Only, Structured Fields for UI Elements
nodes.norm_label: adr-13: sanitized rendering only, structured fields for ui elements
nodes.rationale: Model-boundary injection defense does not stop tainted text re-entering at the render boundary: raw-HTML rendering of source-derived text would let a crafted client PDF forge citation chips or authority badges even when the model was never fooled. Chips and badges are populated only from structured ingestion fields.

nodes.label: ADR-14: Model-Boundary Prompt-Injection Defense
nodes.rationale: Client-uploaded documents are untrusted input that reaches LLM calls. Retrieved client content is inserted as clearly delimited, labeled data and the system prompt treats it as reference material only; a synthetic injection corpus must pass 100% in CI before any real client document is ingested.

nodes.label: ADR-2: Bi-Temporal Fact Validity
nodes.rationale: Valid-time-only fields were mislabeled bi-temporal. Tracking transaction time as well lets the system answer both 'what was the rule on date X' and 'what did TaxCite believe on date Y' — the relevant question under source corrections, delayed ingestion and retroactive legislation.

nodes.label: ADR-5: Shared Corpus + Per-Tenant Namespace
nodes.rationale: One shared statute/case-law index with query-layer isolation trades a small blast radius (a misconfigured filter) for large storage and compute savings; compensated by a 0-tolerance cross-tenant leakage test.

nodes.label: PII Redaction Ordering as a CI Invariant
nodes.norm_label: pii redaction ordering as a ci invariant
nodes.rationale: Redaction runs in request preprocessing before any span is emitted, never as a post-hoc filter on stored traces; a CI test plants a canary PII-shaped string and asserts it never appears raw in exported spans.

nodes.label: Client-Upload Threat Model
nodes.rationale: File types are allowlisted and anything else rejected outright rather than best-effort parsed; failed OCR/table extraction is marked 'extraction failed — excluded from retrieval' rather than silently indexed as reliable source text.

nodes.label: TaxCite
nodes.rationale: A citation-grounded RAG system for compound US federal tax questions; every claim must carry a citation verified against its source, because an unretrieved LLM hallucinates section numbers and expiration dates.

nodes.label: Goals G1-G6 (research time, seat displacement, groundedness, gates, cost, leakage)
nodes.norm_label: goals g1-g6 (research time, seat displacement, groundedness, gates, cost, leakage)

nodes.label: Open Questions (embedding, LLM provider, frontend, backup storage, market scope)
nodes.norm_label: open questions (embedding, llm provider, frontend, backup storage, market scope)

nodes.label: Renee (Enrolled Agent persona)
nodes.rationale: Sole named persona; 3-person practice, ~400 clients, spends 25-40 min per question cross-referencing sources

nodes.label: Eval Harness as a Standalone Deliverable
nodes.norm_label: eval harness as a standalone deliverable
nodes.rationale: Published as its own artifact rather than internal QA; metrics are reported separately rather than collapsed into one groundedness number, and failure analysis is published alongside successes.

nodes.label: Confirmed Intent
nodes.rationale: Upstream of the PRD and tech doc, which stay authoritative for how. The audience is interviewers and engineering reviewers; the piece is a production-grade portfolio artifact, not a product for real customers.

nodes.label: Stanford Legal-AI Hallucination Rate (17-33%)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately softened from a 'floor to beat' to an external reference point: different products, question distributions and labeling methodologies mean the number is not apples-to-apples. The primary comparison is TaxCite's own closed-book baseline.

nodes.label: Cost Model and Budget Governance (§4.1)
nodes.rationale: Cost was the least-specified constraint despite 'free tier' being load-bearing. Worst case is ~5 LLM calls per query under a hard <$50/mo ceiling; caching full verified sub-answers is the primary lever for staying under it.

hyperedges.label: Phase A Decisions Settled by Measurement
Measurements That Overturned a Stated Intuition
